variants.direction:
Design L04 as a compact sculpted central body with an oval-to-trapezoidal cross section: a modest convex upper shoulder, a definite central waist in plan, and a fuller lower keel that tapers up into the stern. The center hatch follows a small clean roof plateau. Avoid tall dorsal fins on THIS variant.
Give the fan wings three broad, thin, clearly differentiated wedge sectors per side. Their outer contour forms a strong swept stepped arc, with crisp truncated points and one large shallow inset field per leaf. Solid crescent-like root saddles grow naturally out of the tapered lower shoulder; one clean angular relief cut reveals each enclosed hinge seat. Body lines continue into the fan leaves. Keep the entire deployed wing silhouette large relative to the body. The stern resolves into two compact stacked rounded-faceted engine collars and a small integrated transverse terminal plane. This should read as an elegant, broad, mechanically plausible Liberty raider with compact volume, not a transport.
Header exactly: "LI PIR ELITE — L04".
variants.prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Create a new concept for a PIRATE LIBERTY ELITE heavy fighter from Freelancer. It must belong unmistakably to the Liberty fleet. This design study prioritizes silhouette, volume distribution and coherent structural lines.

REFERENCES: 1 is the exact immutable li_pir_elite cockpit in four views. 2 is the complete original in deployed flight. 3 shows the actual three-leaf fan mechanism, with FLIGHT in the LEFT column. 4 compares the whole Liberty fleet without textures: study its axial bodies, changing cross sections, thin transverse collars and shaped planes. 5 is the original Mercenary Elite Fighter art, for flowing lines and fan proportions ONLY; its DIFFERENT short high cockpit must not be copied.

COCKPIT: reproduce reference 1's original elongated rounded capsule, surrounding shell, blue-grey glazing, thin window frames and native mounting. The large side panes, central roof pane, small rear side panes and rounded glazed nose all remain. The cockpit itself is the nose, projecting ahead of three relatively thin transverse collar flanges. Keep its original physical scale, approximately a quarter of total ship length. Do not turn it into a jet canopy on a beak, bury it in armor, change the glazing or put a pointed nose in front.

PROPORTIONS: this is a broad-winged fighter, with a narrow but properly three-dimensional central core. Deployed wingspan is approximately 90–100% of total ship length; the central body's width is only about 25% of that span. Look closely at reference 2's TOP view. Keep the stock ship's overall height and depth, with a meaningful belly and inclined wings. The body must not become a long thick rectangular armor block with tiny wings. Thin wing planes do not mean a vertically flattened ship.

LIBERTY FORM: coherent fore-aft axis, an original rounded nose contrasted with angular fan planes, an intentional progression of cross sections and a few graceful long lines. Give the central hull a designed volume, where planar facets turn into tapered shoulders and a narrowing stern. Changes in section must be visible in both top and side views. The broad three-sector wings are a leading part of the silhouette. Large calm surfaces coexist with well-defined hinge seats, recessed functional fields and medium-sized mechanical joints. The character comes from the shape and intersections of planes, not an ornamental grille stuck on a box.

MECHANICS: each side has THREE connected overlapping solid fan leaves, broadly spread in flight and inclined downward around 22.5 degrees. They rotate inward/back to nest for docking as reference 3 shows. Shape their angular outlines and enclosed root attachments, keeping actual separation between moving sections. Two long cargo doors occupy the central top deck behind the collar: two panels side by side, a fore-aft center seam, hinges along their outer long edges. Leave this roof and its outward/upward opening sweep clear. Rear structures begin BEHIND the doors. Exactly TWO aft-facing engines stacked VERTICALLY on the centerline; the upper is larger. In strict top view the lower engine is occluded, not drawn beside the upper.

PIRATE CHARACTER: practical altered wing-root sockets, two or three integrated replacement hull sections, restrained imperfect repair joins and modified cut-in profiles. Balanced main silhouette. Dull oxide red/brown with pale worn metal replacement areas, charcoal functional recesses, original blue-grey windows. Light weathering so contours remain legible. Medium detail with purposeful mechanical forms; not bare primitive boxes. No exposed pipes, scaffolding, open rod frames, horns, skulls, flags, gold ornament, tiny rivets, massive perimeter armor or dense repetitive greebles.

PRESENTATION: one coherent design on a pale neutral landscape production concept sheet. Large clear three-quarter perspective above, whole ship fully visible, both broad wings readable, nose LEFT. Below: a true SIDE profile and a true TOP view of the SAME design in deployed flight, with matching cabin, outline and panel placement. Use a crisp industrial-design painting with controlled shading and clean material blocks. No scenery, background story, dramatic lighting or dirt hiding the form. Only the specified header plus "SIDE" and "TOP".

Design L04 as a compact sculpted central body with an oval-to-trapezoidal cross section: a modest convex upper shoulder, a definite central waist in plan, and a fuller lower keel that tapers up into the stern. The center hatch follows a small clean roof plateau. Avoid tall dorsal fins on THIS variant.
Give the fan wings three broad, thin, clearly differentiated wedge sectors per side. Their outer contour forms a strong swept stepped arc, with crisp truncated points and one large shallow inset field per leaf. Solid crescent-like root saddles grow naturally out of the tapered lower shoulder; one clean angular relief cut reveals each enclosed hinge seat. Body lines continue into the fan leaves. Keep the entire deployed wing silhouette large relative to the body. The stern resolves into two compact stacked rounded-faceted engine collars and a small integrated transverse terminal plane. This should read as an elegant, broad, mechanically plausible Liberty raider with compact volume, not a transport.
Header exactly: "LI PIR ELITE — L04".

variants.direction:
Design L05 with a narrow central hull and a taller, sculpted rear silhouette. The body develops from an oval neck through crisp oblique shoulder facets, then contracts toward the stacked engines. Give the rear third a short swept dorsal crest made of TWO nested solid geometric planes, inspired by Liberty elite2, with a strong clipped top and visible offset between the planes. This crest rises BEHIND the cargo hatch and adds height without thickening the whole fuselage; it is a shaped aircraft-like surface, not a masonry tower.
The three broad fan sectors per side have a more forward-reaching first leaf and a deeper concave notch between the outer tip steps than L04. Their broad root attaches through an oblique solid shell transition with a recessed hinge disk, so the wing seems to flow out of the body rather than hang from a bulky bracket. Connect lower fuselage and stern with one rising angular keel line, keeping full body depth. Give the stern a pronounced narrowing before two vertically stacked engines, with a pair of short swept solid flanges framing their connection. Sparse replacement sections and roughened hinge housings express the pirate refit. Preserve the broad deployed span.
Header exactly: "LI PIR ELITE — L05". Upper profile uses solid thin planes rather than enlarged hull walls.

Critical hatch drawing instruction: the TOP view has the nose pointing LEFT. Draw the two long hatch panels one ABOVE the other on the page, each extending horizontally toward the tail. A single HORIZONTAL central seam parallel to the long body axis separates them. Never draw them end-to-end along the length. In perspective show two parallel long skinny doors, not two short square lids. Keep the sides of the core deep enough to retain the native height; the narrow core is not a thin flat slab.

user_direction: Два концепта по новой схеме после изучения всего флота Liberty. Предыдущие формы слишком коробчатые и тяжёлые; потеряли стиль. Не уменьшать высоту, сохранять родную кабину.
scope: Raster concepts only. No modeling selection or installation. L03 is rejected and is not an input.
